# Exploring targets

Keep the native demo running and attach to it:

```text
[0x00000000]> Froj frida://attach/local//native_demo
{"ok":true,"result":{"action":"attach","pid":46117,"resumed":false,"state":"attached"}}
```

## Devices

```text
[0x00000000]> Frdj
{"ok":true,"result":{"devices":[{"id":"local","name":"Local System","type":"local","lost":false},{"id":"socket","name":"Local Socket","type":"remote","lost":false},{"id":"barebone","name":"GDB Remote Stub","type":"remote","lost":false},{"id":"emulator-5554","name":"Android Emulator 5554","type":"usb","lost":false}]}}
```

`Frdj` lists every device frida knows: the local system, remote stubs and
the USB emulator. `lost` reports whether a device disappeared.

## Processes and applications

```text
[0x00000000]> Frpj frida://list/usb//
{"ok":true,"result":{"processes":[{"pid":1,"name":"init"},...]}}
```

The URI selects the device. `list/usb//` means "the single USB device". The
demo app appears as `FridaMin`: the process name is the app label:

```text
{"pid":2812,"name":"FridaMin"}
```

Applications are enumerated with `Fraj`, giving identifiers and display
names:

```text
[0x00000000]> Fraj frida://apps/usb//
{"ok":true,"result":{"apps":[{"identifier":"com.android.calendar","name":"Calendar","pid":0},...,{"identifier":"re.frida.minapp","name":"FridaMin","pid":2812}]}}
```

`pid` is nonzero only when the app is running.

## Modules

```text
[0x00000000]> FrMj
{"ok":true,"result":{"modules":[{"name":"native_demo","base":"0x5c95c4680000","size":16448,"path":".../native_demo"},...],"cached":false}}
```

The agent caches the module list. `cached` reports whether the reply came
from the cache. Pass any argument to force a fresh enumeration:

```text
[0x00000000]> FrMj refresh
```

## Exports, imports and symbols

```text
[0x00000000]> FrEj native_demo
{"ok":true,"result":{"module":"native_demo","exports":[{"type":"variable","name":"stdout","address":"0x5c95c4681020","size":8},{"type":"variable","name":"stdin","address":"0x5c95c4681030","size":8}]}}
```

Only a few exports on a small program. Imports point into libc:

```text
[0x00000000]> FrIj native_demo
{"ok":true,"result":{"module":"native_demo","imports":[{"type":"function","name":"puts","module":"/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6","address":"0x795091c87cc0","slot":"0x5c95c4680fa0"},...]}}
```

Symbols are what the native chapters rely on: actual names and addresses.

```text
[0x00000000]> FrSj native_demo
{"ok":true,"result":{"module":"native_demo","symbols":[...,{"name":"g_secret","address":"0x5c95c4681010","size":16},...,{"name":"check_key","address":"0x5c95c467e209","size":48},...]}}
```

`check_key`, `bump_counter`, `g_secret`, `g_attempts`: everything is there
because the demo was built with `-g` and not stripped.

### Filtering module output

Module names are platform-specific: the Android C library is `libc.so`,
while the native Linux demo uses `libc.so.6`.

On the Android target:

```text
[0x00000000]> FrEj libnative.so~JNI
{"ok":true,"result":{"module":"libnative.so","exports":[{"type":"function","name":"JNI_OnLoad","address":"0x7adf675eed30","size":427}]}}
```

The rizin `~` operator filters rendered **lines**. Because `FrEj` emits
one complete JSON envelope on one line, `FrEj libc.so.6~open` keeps or
discards the entire envelope. It does not select individual array entries.
Use the shell pipe operator and `jq` for a readable, JSON-aware filter:

```text
[0x00000000]> FrEj libc.so.6 | jq -r '.result.exports[] | select(.name | contains("open")) | [.name, .address] | @tsv'
_IO_popen	0x73e276887990
sem_open	0x73e2768a44c0
fts64_open	0x73e276918720
__open_nocancel	0x73e27691c9a0
opendir	0x73e2768ed680
fts_open	0x73e276918720
```

The exact addresses and duplicate symbol entries depend on the libc build.
On Android, replace `libc.so.6` with `libc.so` after checking the module
name with `FrMj`.

## Memory ranges

```text
[0x00000000]> FrRj
{"ok":true,"result":{"ranges":[{"base":"0x5c95c4680000","size":16448,"protection":"r-x","file":{"path":".../native_demo","offset":0,"size":16448}},...],"cached":false}}
```

Ranges carry `base`, `size`, `protection` and the backing `file` when there
is one. Like modules, ranges are cached and refreshed on demand:

```text
[0x00000000]> FrRj refresh
```

## Threads

```text
[0x00000000]> Frtj
{"ok":true,"result":{"threads":[{"id":46117,"state":"waiting","context":{"rip":"0x7ffc580d0f9a",...}}]}}
```

Each thread reports its `id`, `state` and a serialized register `context`
with the full CPU state (`rip`, `rax`, ... `sp`, `pc`). On Android, threads
created by the framework also carry an `entrypoint`.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Try

On the emulator target, list modules and find `libnative.so`, then grep its
exports for `JNI`. List its ranges and its threads.
:::
